subject: Next steps & prompt bank upload — Redwood eval for BrightLane
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@brightlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps & prompt bank upload — Redwood eval for BrightLane

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for your time earlier — good conversation and helped clarify BrightLane's top priorities for the evaluation (accuracy on user-facing answers, latency under 200ms P50 for short queries, and predictable token cost). Quick recap and suggested next steps: 

- Deliverables we need from BrightLane: a ~200-query prompt bank (representative user queries + 15–20 edge cases) and a short note on PII/data sensitivity per query. We can accept CSV or the attached template (prompt_submission_template.xlsx).
- Redwood deliverables: model recommendations and a benchmark summary for similar retrieval+answering workloads (attached: model_benchmarks_summary.pdf).
- Timeline suggestion: prompt upload by EOD Wednesday (May 12) so we can run an initial eval the following week and share results by May 19.

Model recommendations (initial):
- redwood-gpt-13b-qa-v2 (recommended): strong factuality, optimized KV cache, quantization-ready.
- community-gpt-7b-instruct (fallback): lower cost, slightly higher hallucination risk on rare entities.

Security/redaction note: if any prompts contain customer PII, flag those rows in the upload and we will apply our redaction/handle-as-sensitive workflow. See our quick redaction guide attached (redwood_prompt_redaction_guidelines.md) and the upload form link below.

Upload: https://forms.redwood.ai/prompt-submission/BRIGHTLANE-UPLOAD
Benchmarks: https://drive.redwood.ai/benchmarks/rdw-vs-open-2027#brightlane

Would you be able to confirm the dataset owners who will upload and whether BrightLane prefers SSO access to our shared folder or a presigned upload link?

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa on the eval plan once we have the sample prompts.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwood.ai]

[Attachment: model_benchmarks_summary.pdf (summary PDF)]
[Attachment: prompt_submission_template.xlsx (spreadsheet template)]

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@brightlane.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightLane Data Team <data@brightlane.com>
Date: Wed, 06 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & prompt bank upload — Redwood eval for BrightLane

Thanks, Evelyn — appreciate the clear recap.

We can deliver an initial 200 prompts, but quick heads-up on data sensitivity: about 12 of the prompts are user-reported issues that include personal identifiers (email or partial account IDs). We need guidance on redaction best practices so we don't break the semantics of the query.

I attached a small test export (brightlane_customer_prompts.csv) that includes a few representative rows — not the full set — would you and Marissa confirm if that format works? Also, we prefer a presigned upload rather than SSO for the initial pass.

Uploading: we can send the full set by May 11 if the format and redaction approach look good.

Thanks,
Sarah Nguyen
Product Lead — Search & Answers, BrightLane
sarah.nguyen@brightlane.com

[Attachment: brightlane_customer_prompts.csv (CSV sample)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@brightlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 07 May 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & prompt bank upload — Redwood eval for BrightLane

Sarah — thanks for the sample. Marissa and I reviewed the CSV and it looks like a good shape to start. A few concrete redaction tips that preserve intent while removing PII: 

- Replace email-like tokens with [EMAIL] and account IDs with [ACCOUNT_ID:n] where n is a short hash (keeps entity uniqueness).
- For queries that depend on entity formats (e.g., credit card last4), replace the numeric portion with Xs but keep the surrounding context.
- Mark rows with high sensitivity in the 'sensitivity' column (Low/Medium/High). Marissa: see the sample mapping we used on lines 8–12 in the CSV.

Model guidance: to set expectations before the eval run — we’ll test the two model families I mentioned across three slices: short help queries, multi-turn clarification prompts, and edge-case mentions (rare entity names). Our recommended config for the initial run:

- redwood-gpt-13b-qa-v2: int8 quant, batch size 8, max tokens 256.
- community-gpt-7b-instruct: float16, batch size 16 for throughput tests.

We will also run a small quality-regression baseline using your historical top-100 queries to ensure no performance drop vs your current system. That’s why we asked for the top queries — if you can flag them, it speeds the regression checks.

Proposed next steps:
1) BrightLane confirms uploader and agrees to presigned link -> we’ll send presigned link by EOD.
2) Upload 200 prompts by Tue May 11.
3) Redwood runs initial eval May 12–14, share benchmarks by May 19.

Marissa, can you add the exact job that will run the regression checks and the expected artifact (CSV/JSON results + example outputs)?

Best,
Evelyn

[Attachment: redwood_prompt_redaction_guidelines.md (guidelines)]

Sarah — quick note from me to align on monitoring and the upload path: 

- We’ll send a presigned upload link (one-time use, 72-hour expiry) to the uploader you confirm. Use that for the full CSV/Excel set. Link: https://files.redwood.ai/upload/presigned/BRL-2027-0543
- For the regression checks, we run a baseline job that outputs a CSV of metrics (accuracy, F1, hallucination-rate) plus up to 10 example outputs per metric bucket. The artifact will be shared in the same Drive folder.
- Please flag the top ~30 priority queries in a column called 'priority' with values 1..30 — that lets us seed the regression suite.

If you’re comfortable, we’ll also spin a canary of redwood-gpt-13b-qa-v2 on a small traffic slice for a week after the eval to validate latency in your environment (no production traffic). We’ll require an NDA addendum for that step — I can route through legal if needed.

Thanks — looking forward to the upload.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
